#### Registered Engineering-Bound Headline Uncertainty

The shaft and finite-ground results above are conditional on synthetic grip,
shaft, and support properties. A point count alone does not show whether the
headline survives plausible engineering variation. The registered uncertainty
campaign therefore repeats the complete production atlases at nominal and at
low and high one-at-a-time corners. It does not replace either atlas with a
reduced surrogate. Every affected corner retains both native engines, complete
velocity reversal, the registered timestep refinement pair, pathway
killswitches, the same 4--50 ms horizons, and the same 5% peak-load and
dissipated-work matching rule.

The design contains one nominal case and 18 corners over nine axes. Grip total
stiffness is scaled to 0.6 and 1.4 of nominal, and grip total damping to 0.5 and
1.5. First bending frequency is scaled to 0.8 and 1.2; torsional stiffness to
0.64 and 1.44, corresponding to 0.8 and 1.2 frequency-scale endpoints when
inertia is fixed; and shaft damping ratio spans 0.009--0.036 around 0.018.
Ground translation stiffness, translation damping, intrinsic-free-moment
stiffness, and intrinsic-free-moment damping each span 0.5--1.5 of nominal.
These are transparent engineering bounds, not measured distributions of
players, grips, shafts, footwear, or surfaces.

The estimand is deliberately narrow. For each corner, the campaign reports the
number of coupled-versus-reference cells that still satisfy the unchanged
load--work comparability screen and its change from the nominal 126/384 shaft
and 0/384 ground counts. A change in count means that comparability
classification is sensitive to that parameter. It is not an effect size, a
probability, evidence that a pathway improves clubhead speed, or permission to
interpret unmatched speed differences. A ground corner moving above zero, for
example, would identify cells eligible for the already registered matched
comparison; it would not establish a ground-use benefit.

![Articulated Headline Sensitivity Across Registered Engineering Bounds](figures/fig_articulated_headline_uncertainty.pdf){#fig-articulated-headline-uncertainty width=100%}

Figure @fig-articulated-headline-uncertainty shows low and high count changes
separately for the shaft and finite-ground screens. A failed corner remains in
the machine-readable record and appears explicitly rather than being removed
from the denominator. The governed record is available as
[`data/articulated_headline_uncertainty.json`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/docs/research/proximal_distal_energy_transfer/data/articulated_headline_uncertainty.json),
and the executable design is available as
[`articulated_headline_uncertainty.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/scripts/research/proximal_distal_energy/articulated_headline_uncertainty.py).

This one-at-a-time design exposes first-order fragility and adverse numerical
corners, but it does not estimate parameter interactions or a joint uncertainty
distribution. Survival across these bounds remains qualification only for the
declared synthetic model. Equipment calibration, participant-specific contact
and anatomy, unilateral foot contact, impact, full-downswing delivery, and
held-out bilateral-wrench validation remain required before any human or
coaching interpretation.
